All Google figures below are from the captured store, coverage `covered` and density **COMPLETE** for both quarters (Q1 2026: 88 of 90 days; Q1 2025: 86 of 90 — the absent days read as no-activity, not gaps). Settled through **2026-08-14**. Both are historical windows, so there's no live counterpart to set alongside them.

Two things to state up front: **no revenue source attributes to Google** in either quarter, so the only ROAS I can give you here is **ad-attributed** (Google's own conversionValue ÷ spend) — it is not the dashboard card ROAS. And the `conversion_action` family failed to load twice this turn — the live fetch errored, and the captured read timed out on our side. So I could not verify how conversions are being counted in either quarter. That is a failure on our end, not a statement about the account, and it matters below.

---

# Verdict up front

**You spent 27% more and got 63% fewer conversions. But the account didn't get worse at advertising — it got worse at allocating.** The single campaign in Q1 2026 that's shaped like Q1 2025's winner actually *beat* Q1 2025's winner. It received 14% of the budget.

---

## Account level

| | Q1 2025 | Q1 2026 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $14,964.01 | **$19,076.96** | **+$4,112.95 (+27.5%)** |
| Impressions | 1,398,279 | 5,608,479 | +301% |
| Clicks | 11,461 | 126,893 | +1,007% |
| CTR | 0.82% | 2.26% | +176% |
| CPC | $1.31 | $0.15 | −89% |
| Conversions | 255.4 | **93.8** | **−63.3%** |
| CPA | $58.59 | **$203.38** | **+247%** |
| Ad-attributed value | $61,085.98 | $25,007.02 | −59.1% |
| Ad-attributed ROAS | **4.08x** | **1.31x** | **−67.9%** |

**Ignore the CTR and CPC lines.** They look like a triumph and they are a mix artifact — see below.

---

## What actually changed: structure

Q1 2025 was **two campaigns**. Q1 2026 was **six**.

**Q1 2025**
| Campaign | Spend | Conv | CPA | Ad ROAS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales-Performance Max-Evergreen | $14,297.98 | 244.6 | $58.45 | **4.14x** |
| Sales-Search-8 | $666.01 | 11.1 | $59.80 | 2.88x |

One evergreen PMax carried **95.5% of spend and 95.6% of conversions** at 4.14x.

**Q1 2026**
| Campaign | Spend | % of spend | Conv | CPA | Ad ROAS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Website traffic-Performance Max-Feb '26 | $2,747.38 | 14.4% | 35.8 | $76.81 | **4.50x** |
| Spring Sale \| Sales \| PMax \| 2026 | $4,841.82 | 25.4% | 48.0 | $100.83 | 2.12x |
| Spring Sale \| Sales \| Search \| 2026 | $5,531.77 | 29.0% | 10.0 | **$551.75** | **0.43x** |
| Demand Gen - Jan '26 | $4,085.64 | 21.4% | **0** | — | **0.00x** |
| Spring Sale \| Sales \| Display \| 2026 | $1,870.36 | 9.8% | **0** | — | **0.00x** |
| Spring Sale Competitors \| Search \| 2026 | $0.00 | 0% | 0 | — | — |

---

## The three findings

**1. Your best campaign this year is better than your best campaign last year — and it's starved.**
`Website traffic-Performance Max-Feb '26` returned **4.50x on $2,747**, beating the 2025 Evergreen's 4.14x on a $76.81 CPA vs $58.45. That is the same campaign shape doing the same job, and it works. It got **14.4% of the quarter's budget**. The 2025 equivalent got 95.5%. Whatever else is true, the machine that produced Q1 2025 still runs.

**2. 31% of Google spend produced zero attributed conversions.**
Demand Gen ($4,085.64) and Display ($1,870.36) = **$5,956.00 with 0 conversions and $0 attributed value**. Demand Gen alone bought **115,026 clicks at $0.04** — that's 90.6% of every click in the quarter and 78.6% of every impression. *That* is where your 2.26% CTR and $0.15 CPC come from. Strip those two campaigns out and the real picture of your converting spend is:

| Converting spend only | Q1 2025 | Q1 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Spend | $14,964.01 | $13,120.97 |
| CTR | 0.82% | 0.89% |
| CPC | $1.31 | $1.64 |
| Conversions | 255.4 | 93.8 |
| CPA | $58.59 | $139.85 |
| Ad ROAS | 4.08x | **1.91x** |

So on comparable money — $13,121 vs $14,964, down 12% — you got 63% fewer conversions. The efficiency loss is real, it's just half the size the headline suggests. **⚠ Caveat I can't clear:** because the conversion_action read failed both ways, I cannot tell you whether Demand Gen and Display genuinely converted zero times or whether their conversion actions simply aren't being counted into these campaigns. A flat 0.0 across 118,897 clicks is the shape of a tracking/attribution question as much as a performance one. I'd resolve that before acting on it.

**3. Spring Sale Search is the worst line item in the account and the second-largest.**
$5,531.77 at **0.43x**, a **$551.75 CPA**, and a **$4.36 CPC** — more than triple Sales-Search-8's $2.92 in Q1 2025, on a 3.93% CTR that says the ads are relevant but the auction is expensive. You're paying competitor-auction prices and closing at 0.79%. This ties directly to the negative-keyword work from earlier in the thread; that list was built off 2026 YTD search terms and this campaign is a large part of why the tail was so expensive.

Also: `Spring Sale Competitors | Sales | Search | 2026` took 235 impressions and $0.00 — it effectively never ran.

---

## Business context around it

Store revenue (Shopify, capture COMPLETE 90/90 days both quarters): **$69,400.30 in Q1 2025 → $60,854.29 in Q1 2026, −12.3%** — against Google spend up 27.5%.

⚠ I can only give you the **covered portion** of the Q1 2026 cross-platform picture, not a window total: **Meta captured nothing across all 90 days of Q1 2026** despite capture reaching back to 2023-06-21. That is an unfilled window, **not $0** — I can't confirm Meta was dark, so I can't state blended Q1 2026 spend or blended ROAS. Q1 2025 is fully covered and had $35,999.19 of Meta spend alongside Google.

GA4 sessions ran **71,175 → 168,519** (+137%), which is the Demand Gen click flood arriving. Both are per-day sums of captured rows and won't tie exactly to what you see in GA4's own range view. Revenue fell while sessions more than doubled — that traffic isn't buying.

---

## What I'd do

1. **Move budget into the Feb '26 PMax shape.** It's the only asset in the account clearing 4x, and it's proven at $2,747. Scale it deliberately and watch CPA past ~$100 — the Spring PMax at 2.12x is the same campaign type with worse economics, so the shape alone isn't the magic; find what differs between them before you assume it scales linearly.
2. **Resolve the zero-conversion question before you cut.** $5,956 with a flat 0.0 needs the conversion-action audit first. If tracking is fine, Demand Gen and Display are a clean $5,956 to redeploy. If it isn't, you'd be cutting on a measurement artifact.
3. **Cap Spring Sale Search or restructure it.** At $4.36 CPC and 0.43x it's losing roughly $3,141 of attributed value against its spend. Negatives plus a CPC ceiling, or pause it into the PMax.
4. **Arithmetic worth seeing, not a forecast:** Q1 2026's $19,077 at Q1 2025's efficiency would have returned ~$77,834 of attributed value instead of $25,007. That gap is allocation, not market.

One thing I can't tell you: I have no record of *why* the structure changed between these quarters — LoraMer doesn't capture account-change history, so I can't confirm any restructure, launch, or strategy shift or when it happened. If you tell me when the Demand Gen and Spring Sale builds went in, I can cut the data around those dates properly.

Meta conversion figures cited for Q1 2025 are account-level historical values — directionally accurate but they may not reconcile perfectly with campaign-level conversion numbers; Meta spend, clicks and impressions are exact.

You didn't name a year, so I used **Q2 2026 (Apr 1 – Jun 30)**, the most recent complete quarter, and pulled **Q2 2025** alongside it since the direction of the gap flipped. Both are historical windows, so there's no live counterpart — everything below is captured/settled through **2026-08-14**.

### The comparison

| | Q2 2026 | Q2 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| **Shopify net sales** (refund-adjusted, excl. shipping & tax) | **$9,906.00** | **$117,840.00** |
| **GA4 revenue** | **$11,843.00** | **$115,634.87** |
| Delta (GA4 − Shopify) | **+$1,937.00 (+19.6%)** | −$2,205.13 (−1.9%) |
| GA4 transactions | 51 | 542 |

**Shopify is the canonical figure** in both quarters — store beats GA in revenue precedence, so $9,906 is what the dashboard card shows for Q2 2026. GA4 is the second, independent measurement, not a competing total.

### Why they differ — and why the sign flipped

**Q2 2026: GA4 reads 19.6% high, and refunds are most of it.** Shopify booked **$1,295.11 in refunds across 4 orders** — 11.5% of gross sales. GA4's captured refund amount for the same window is **$0.00**, meaning those refunds never made it back into the property. Add refunds back and reconcile the basis difference:

| Step | Q2 2026 |
|---|---|
| Gross sales | $11,227.00 |
| − Discounts | $60.00 |
| = Net sales (Shopify basis) | $9,906.00 |
| + Taxes | $163.78 |
| + Shipping | $75.00 |
| = Total sales | $10,144.78 |
| + Refunds added back | $1,295.11 |
| **= Comparable-to-GA4 basis** | **$11,439.89** |
| GA4 revenue | $11,843.00 |
| **Unexplained residual** | **$403.11 (3.4%)** |

So the headline 19.6% gap is really **two basis differences plus ~3% of genuine attribution noise**: Shopify net excludes shipping and tax and subtracts refunds; GA4's purchase event captures order value at checkout and never gets the refund signal. A 3.4% residual on 51 transactions is one order's worth of timing — a session that crossed a day boundary, or a purchase counted on click-date rather than order-date.

**Q2 2025 was the opposite problem.** GA4 ran **1.9% below** Shopify on 542 transactions — the normal shape, where blocked pixels and consent-declined sessions cost GA4 a slice of real orders. Refunds were negligible that quarter ($364 across 3 orders, 0.3% of gross), so nothing masked the under-count.

The flip isn't a tracking regression — it's **volume collapse changing which error dominates**. At $117.8k of quarterly revenue, GA4's structural under-count is the visible force. At $9.9k with an 11.5% refund rate, a single refunded castle sofa swamps it. Shopify revenue is down **91.6% year over year** in Q2, and that is the finding that actually matters here.

1. **Wire refunds into GA4.** You're currently blind to $1,295 of returned revenue in the analytics property, and at this volume that's a fifth of your reported number. Any GA4-based ROAS you or the client look at for 2026 is overstated by roughly that much.
2. **Treat GA4 as directional only for 2026.** Use Shopify net for anything that touches money. The two agreed within 2% at scale; they will not agree at this volume.
3. **The Q2 2026 refund rate needs a look on its own** — 4 refunded orders against ~$11.2k gross is a materially different return profile than Q2 2025's 0.3%, and on this few orders it's worth knowing whether it's one product or one fulfillment problem.
